text:
sachin: heads up — canary rollout of model v3.7.0 is causing p99 token latency to jump from ~120ms to ~420ms for short-chat traffic (seq <= 128). noticed around 09:12 UTC.
marina: saw the alert, digging in. did we change tokenizer or decoding config in this build?
sachin: tokenizer changed — switched to bpe-merge-v2 to reduce OOVs. config shows max_length unchanged.
leo: dumping per-request seq len histogram for canary vs baseline:
```
canary seq_len percentiles: 50=32 90=96 99=184
baseline seq_len percentiles: 50=30 90=92 99=130
```
leo: 99th shifted a lot — v3.7.0 produces more subtokens -> higher tail.
amanda: KV cache is per-step growth; if seq lengths jump, memory traffic increases and batching heuristics might pick different kernels. check kernel selection logs.
sachin: pulled runtime profile for one hotspot instance:
```
[2026-02-26T09:14:02Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_nc16x16_gemm_fast for seq_len=128 batch=4
[2026-02-26T09:14:02Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_generic for seq_len=192 batch=2
[2026-02-26T09:14:02Z] kv_cache: active_items=192 avg_kv_bytes=1.6MB
[2026-02-26T09:14:02Z] batcher: flush_reason=time budget exceeded (latency SLO)
```
leo: the selector fell back to a generic kernel for >160 tokens which is ~3-4x slower for our model. that aligns with p99 jump.
marina: any evidence of KV cache thrashing causing GPU memory alloc/free?
amanda: yes, infra logs show elevated cudaMalloc/cudaFree churn on the canary hosts. sample: `cudaMalloc 38ms` spikes coincident with increased seq len.
infra-bot: Deploy job 9812 -> canary v3.7.0 on pool "canary-gpu-a" completed at 09:11:54 UTC (sha: ab12cd).
ci-bot: Canary reached 10% traffic at 09:12:30 UTC.
leo: also saw batching heuristic changes — dynamic packer now tries to pack by tokens, but with wider tail it creates smaller batches more frequently which increases per-token overhead.
sachin: ok immediate mitigation: 1) rollback canary traffic to v3.6.4 2) add routing rule to pin short chats to v3.6.4 3) add temporary kernel policy to prioritize fast gemm for seq <= 256 while we investigate.
marina: implemented routing pin for short-chat (route id r-short-chat) -> v3.6.4, pushed at 09:18 UTC.
amanda: I can push kernel policy change to prefer tuned gemm up to 256 tokens, but need a quick perf test.
leo: ran micro-bench on patched kernel policy: p99 token latency drops from 420ms -> 130ms on test instance. results: throughput slightly lower for very long seq (>512) but our short-chat traffic wins.
sachin: rolling back canary to v3.6.4 now and scaling canary down to 0.5.
infra-bot: Traffic switch: v3.7.0 -> v3.6.4 for traffic group canary-g/short-chat at 09:19:30 UTC.
marina: post-rollback metrics look good; p99 back to ~140ms. leaving canary off until root cause fixed.
amanda: follow-ups: (A) coordinate with model team to evaluate tokenizer bpe-merge-v2 producing longer sequences — maybe change merge ops or use overlap heuristics, (B) adjust kernel selector thresholds to consider seq_len distribution skew, (C) batching heuristic: clamp token-based packing when tail variance > 2x to avoid micro-batches, (D) add KV cache warmup / prefix caching metrics and alerts.
leo: I opened perf ticket #INF-1293 with profile artifacts and perf traces. attaching flamegraphs and nvprof output in the ticket.
sachin: owner-wise: leo -> investigate kernel selector fallback logic, amanda -> kernel policy and perf test, marina -> coordinate with model/tokenizer team and add sequence diagnostics to rollout checks. ETA 48h for root cause PRs.
marina: FYI model team Slack: "@models-team we saw v3.7.0 increase subtokenization in certain short prompts causing seq-tail shift and downstream perf issues. can you run a token-length delta test against the baseline and share detokenized examples?"
models-team (via message): acknowledged, we'll run token-diff and report within 24h.
sachin: logging note — add rollout-gate rule: compare canary seq-len 90/99 percentiles vs baseline; fail rollout if 99th increases > 20% without explicit approval.
amanda: lgtm, and add a perf smoke: run a microbench with randomized seqs up to 256 tokens to validate kernel selection behavior pre-rollout.
leo: also propose adding a telemetry metric `kv_cache_alloc_stalls` to detect alloc/free churn. small alert if sustained > 5/min.
marina: thanks all. will schedule a postmortem update tomorrow. :thumbsup:
sachin: great work — low impact to customers thanks to quick routing change and kernel policy patch. closing incident thread here but please add notes to INF-1293 and the rollout checklist.
